mechanical_approach: Differential drive: two driven wheels and one passive rear ball caster. No steering servo is used; left/right wheel speed differences turn the chassis.
defaults: Arduino Uno R3 is selected because this repository has a verified Uno firmware runtime and HC-SR04 timed echo model. The screenshot's controller looks ESP32-like, but the current ESP32 path cannot simulate this sensor behavior.
Indoor, low-speed classroom robot; stop and reverse before a timed differential turn when an obstacle is closer than 25 cm.
Four alkaline AA cells form a nominal 6 V motor pack. USB powers the Uno during development; share ground with the motor driver. A holder is required physically and is not modeled in the catalog.

unresolved: WireUp has no brushed DC motor or ball-caster component types, so the two Pololu motors and caster are documented external integrations and have no circuit pins or per-part 3D exports.
L293D, battery, chassis, wheels, and sensor do not form a vehicle-dynamics simulation in the current runtime. Only the Uno firmware and HC-SR04 timed echo path are in the supported simulator scope.
Blender MCP is not connected in this session; no car chassis, exact component CAD, collision shapes, or Blender exports were generated.
Vehicle mass, center of mass, inertia, tire friction, caster drag, motor heating, driver voltage drop under load, and contact behavior remain unmeasured. Do not claim physical vehicle simulation.
